mainTopic: How a woman can acquire her גט in her own חצר even though her husband has rights in her property: the principle of declining a תקנת חכמים, רבא's idea that the גט and her חצר come 'together', and רבינא's challenge to רבא's comparison with her hand.
overview: The גמרא is asking how a wife can acquire her גט in her own חצר, since her husband has rights in her property. First it explains that a person may decline a תקנת חכמים made for his benefit, like רב הונא's rule that a wife may refuse support and keep her earnings. רבא gives another answer: the גט and her courtyard come to her at the same moment (באין כאחד). רבינא questions the comparison רבא drew to a wife's hand, and רב אשי explains that רבא was really thinking of a slave's hand. A story follows about a dying man. רבא told him to give his wife the place where the גט lay. When רב עיליש challenged this, רבא defended it, at last with the same idea of באין כאחד. Next, עולא and רבי אושעיא argue over whether the woman must be near her courtyard. They explain differently what it means for a חצר to be 'like her hand.' Finally, רב יוסף rules on a גט that landed on a board in a courtyard lent to her. The board's size and height decide whether it is a separate area, and a further limit continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A person may decline a rabbinic enactment made for his benefit
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of a rule: whoever says 'I don't want this תקנת חכמים,' in a case like this one, we listen to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'I don't want the Sages' enactment,' in a case like this, we listen to him.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of a rule the גמרא started quoting just before this point. It says that a person who turns down an enactment the חכמים made for his own good is allowed to do so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some enactments, like the husband's rights in his wife's property, exist to help one side. If the person they were made for gives them up, the enactment no longer applies to him. In context, this helps explain how the husband's rights need not stop the wife's courtyard from acquiring her גט.

keyTerms.meaning: I don't want it / I'm not interested
an enactment made by the Sages
such as this case, a case like this one
we listen to him; his choice is accepted

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a general rule that anyone may ignore any rabbinic law. It only covers enactments made for that person's own benefit, 'such as this.'

phrases.english: "I do not want the enactment of the Sages"
in a case such as this, we listen to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אֶפְשִׁי בְּתַקָּנַת חֲכָמִים כְּגוֹן זוֹ שׁוֹמְעִין לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a statement that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person may give up a rabbinic enactment made for his own benefit, in cases like this one.

steps.title: Which case does 'such as this' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what example the words 'such as this' are pointing to.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'such as this'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short clarifying question about the words 'such as this.' This sets up the next step, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Such as this' suggests a known model case behind the rule. The גמרא wants to name that case so we know how far the rule reaches.

phrases.english: What is meant by "such as this"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי כְּגוֹן זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the example behind the rule in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The model case the words 'such as this' refer to.

steps.title: The model case: a wife may refuse support and keep her earnings
steps.stepSummary: The example is רב הונא in the name of רב: a wife can tell her husband, 'I won't be supported by you, and I won't work for you.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like what רב הונא said in the name of רב. A woman may say to her husband: 'I will not be supported by you, and I will not do work for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by pointing to רב הונא's teaching. A wife may give up her right to be supported so that she keeps her own earnings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים set up a trade: the husband supports his wife and receives what she earns. Since this was made mainly for her benefit, she can turn it down. That is the model for 'such as this': an enactment made for someone's benefit, which that person may decline.

keyTerms.meaning: like the teaching of רב הונא

steps.whatToRemember: 'Such as this' means an enactment made for one person's benefit, like the wife's right to support, which that person may give up.

phrases.english: Like that which רב הונא said in the name of רב,
for רב הונא said in the name of רב:
A woman can say to her husband:
"I will not be supported, and I will not work."
phrases.notes: She gives up his support, and in return she keeps what she earns.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְרַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The model is רב הונא's rule that a wife may refuse support in order to keep her earnings.

steps.title: רבא: the גט and her courtyard come to her at the same moment
steps.stepSummary: רבא compares the case to a wife's hand. Her hand is tied to her husband, yet a גט placed there works, because the גט and her hand come to her together. Her courtyard works the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Is it not true that her hand belongs to her husband? Rather, her גט and her hand come to her at the same moment. Here too, her גט and her courtyard come to her at the same moment.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a different way to explain how a wife's courtyard can acquire her גט. He compares it to her hand, where a גט clearly works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא assumes the husband has a claim on his wife's hand, yet everyone agrees a גט placed in her hand divorces her. That can only be because the divorce and her full ownership arrive together. The same logic lets her courtyard acquire the גט even though her husband had rights in it.

keyTerms.meaning: is that to say? (opens a pointed question)

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that two things 'come together' at one instant lets a single act both release the wife and give her the tool for receiving the release.

phrases.english: רבא said:

phrases.aramaic: אַטּוּ יָדָהּ מִי לָא קַנְיָא לֵיהּ לְבַעַל?!
phrases.english: Is that to say her hand is not owned by the husband?!
phrases.notes: He means: of course it is, and still a גט put in her hand works.

phrases.english: Rather, her גט and her hand come at the same moment;

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי – גִּיטָּהּ וַחֲצֵרָהּ בָּאִין כְּאֶחָד.
phrases.english: here too, her גט and her courtyard come at the same moment.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר אַטּוּ יָדָהּ מִי לָא קַנְיָא לֵיהּ לְבַעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers another solution to the courtyard problem, instead of relying on giving up the enactment.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison to an accepted case (her hand) using the idea that two things arrive at the same moment.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The husband's rights in her courtyard should stop it from acquiring the גט for her.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גט and her full ownership of the courtyard arrive at the same moment, so the courtyard acquires for her.

steps.title: רבינא: the husband never owned her actual hand
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי why רבא found a wife's hand difficult at all. The husband owns her earnings, not her hand itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: Did רבא really find a woman's hand difficult? Granted, the husband owns what her hands produce. But does he own her hand itself?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges the basis of רבא's comparison. He argues that a wife's hand was never a problem, so it cannot serve as the model for her courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband's rights cover only מעשה ידיה, her earnings. Her hand itself belongs fully to her, so a גט in her hand works without any 'coming together' idea. Her courtyard is different, because the husband does have rights in her property, so רבא's comparison seems to fail.

keyTerms.meaning: the work of her hands, her earnings

steps.confusionAlert: Keep apart two things: her earnings (מעשה ידיה), which belong to the husband, and her physical hand, which belongs to her.

phrases.english: רבינא said to רב אשי:

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא – יָד דְּאִשָּׁה קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ?!
phrases.english: Was the hand of a woman difficult for רבא?!
Granted that he owns her earnings,
does he own her hand itself?!
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי רָבָא יָד דְּאִשָּׁה קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the base case רבא relied on in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that her hand is owned by the husband, so that the גט and her hand must come at the same moment.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The husband owns only her earnings, not her hand itself. So a גט in her hand needs no special explanation, and the hand cannot prove anything about her courtyard.

steps.title: It was the slave's hand that bothered רבא
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers רבינא: רבא's real problem was a slave's hand, which belongs to his master. Since a slave still goes free when the שטר is put in his own hand, the document and the hand must come to him together. The same is true of a wife's courtyard and her גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him: What bothered רבא was a slave's hand. According to the opinion that a slave can be freed by a document he receives himself, there is a problem: a slave's hand is like his master's hand! So you must say his document and his hand come to him at the same moment. In the same way, her גט and her courtyard come to her at the same moment.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers רבינא's question from the last step. He explains that רבא was really thinking about a slave's hand, not a wife's hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A slave's body belongs to his master. So when the master puts a שטר שחרור (document of freedom) in the slave's hand, it should be as if the master handed it to himself. Since the slave goes free anyway, the hand and the document must reach the slave together, and רבא uses this same idea for a wife's courtyard.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the hand of his master
By himself (the slave receives it directly)

steps.whatToRemember: The idea of באין כאחד: the slave's hand and his freedom document come to him at the very same moment. רבא uses this to explain how a wife's courtyard can receive her גט.

phrases.english: He said to him: רבא —
phrases.notes: The speaker here is רב אשי, answering רבינא's question from the last step.

phrases.english: it was the hand of a slave that was difficult for him;

phrases.aramaic: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר: בִּשְׁטָר – עַל יְדֵי עַצְמוֹ,
phrases.english: according to the one who says: with a document — by himself,
phrases.notes: This means the opinion that a slave can be freed by a document he receives himself.

phrases.english: a slave's hand is like his master's hand!
Rather, his document and his hand come together at once;

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי נָמֵי – גִּיטָּהּ וַחֲצֵירָהּ בָּאִין כְּאֶחָד.
phrases.english: so too — her גט and her courtyard come together at once.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רָבָא – יַד הָעֶבֶד קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's question in step 5 by changing which hand רבא was talking about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading which case רבא was worried about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבינא thought רבא's problem was a wife's hand, which is not owned by her husband.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא's problem was a slave's hand, which really is owned by the master. The answer is that the hand and the document come together, and the same goes for a wife's courtyard and her גט.

steps.title: A dying man's גט and רבא's ruling
steps.stepSummary: A sick man wrote a גט for his wife just before שבת but did not manage to give it to her. The next day he got worse. רבא told him to give her the spot where the גט was lying, and to have her take possession of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a dying man who wrote a גט for his wife toward evening on ערב שבת, and he did not manage to give it to her. The next day he got much worse. They came before רבא. He said to them: Go tell him to give her ownership of the place where the גט is lying. Then she should go, close the door, open it, and take possession of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case in which רבא used the idea of giving the wife the place where the גט is lying. This story sets up the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man could not hand the גט to his wife directly. So רבא found another way: if she owns the spot where the גט sits, her property receives the גט for her, just like her courtyard. She makes the place hers by closing and opening the door.

keyTerms.meaning: A dangerously sick person, someone on his deathbed

phrases.english: A certain dying man
wrote a גט for his wife
toward evening on ערב שבת,
and he did not manage to give it to her.
The next day, his condition grew much worse.
phrases.notes: Literally, "the world grew strong on him." It means his illness got much worse.

phrases.english: They came before רבא,
he said to them: Go tell him,
he should give her ownership of that place
where the גט is lying,
and she should go and close
phrases.notes: She closes the door of that place.

phrases.english: and open, and take possession of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא שְׁכִיב מְרַע דִּכְתַב לַהּ גִּיטָּא לִדְבֵיתְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells a real case where רבא used the idea that a wife can get her גט through a place she owns.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The husband should give his wife ownership of the place where the גט lies, and she takes possession of it by closing and opening the door.

steps.title: Proof that locking a door takes possession
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up רבא's instruction with a משנה: locking, fencing, or breaking open even a little is enough to take possession of land.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: If someone locked, fenced, or broke open even a little, this counts as taking possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source showing why closing and opening the door is enough for the wife to own the place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Land is acquired through a physical act on it, called חזקה. This משנה teaches that even a small act like locking a door counts, so the wife's closing and opening the door is a valid way to acquire the place.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking possession of land through an action

phrases.english: As we learned: If one locked, fenced in,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in בבא בתרא about how land is acquired.

phrases.aramaic: פָּרַץ כׇּל שֶׁהוּא – הֲרֵי זוֹ חֲזָקָה.
phrases.english: or broke open any amount — this is taking possession.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the method רבא gave in step 7 for the wife to take possession.
steps.raayaObject: That closing and opening the door is a valid way for the wife to acquire the place.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: נעל, גדר, פרץ כל שהוא – הרי זו חזקה.

steps.title: Whatever a wife acquires, her husband acquires
steps.stepSummary: רב עיליש challenges רבא: anything a wife acquires goes to her husband. So the place still belongs to him, and the גט never really left his hands. רבא is embarrassed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עיליש said to רבא: Whatever a woman acquires, her husband acquires! רבא was embarrassed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עיליש attacks רבא's ruling in the dying man's case. רבא has no answer and is embarrassed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While they are married, the husband gets what his wife acquires. So the moment the place becomes hers, it is also his, and the גט is still sitting on the husband's property. It never truly reached her, which is why רבא's plan seems to fail and he is embarrassed.

keyTerms.meaning: Whatever a wife acquires, her husband acquires

steps.confusionAlert: רבא's embarrassment is not the end of the story. In step 11 he answers this very challenge with the idea that her גט and her courtyard come together.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's plan to give the wife the spot where the גט lies is challenged by the rule that whatever a wife acquires, her husband acquires. רבא is embarrassed at first, but steps 10 and 11 defend his ruling.

phrases.english: רב עיליש said to רבא:
Whatever a woman acquires, her husband acquires!
He was embarrassed.
phrases.notes: רבא is the one embarrassed, because he sees his ruling was wrong.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב עִילִישׁ לְרָבָא: מָה שֶׁקָּנְתָה אִשָּׁה קָנָה בַּעְלָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's ruling from step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's instruction to give the wife the place where the גט lies
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A wife's acquisitions belong to her husband. So the place, and the גט in it, stays in the husband's ownership and never reaches her.

steps.title: The woman turns out to be betrothed, so רבא's ruling stands
steps.stepSummary: It comes out that the woman was only an ארוסה. רבא says the rule that a wife's acquisitions belong to her husband was said about a נשואה, not an ארוסה.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end it became clear that she was only betrothed. רבא said: Even if the rule was said about a married woman, would it be said about a betrothed woman?!
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues, and רבא gets an answer to רב עיליש's challenge. The woman was only an ארוסה, so the challenge does not apply to her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב עיליש's attack was that whatever a wife acquires goes to her husband, so the place still belonged to him. That rule only applies once she is fully married (נשואה). An ארוסה's acquisitions stay hers, so the spot really became hers and the גט really left the husband's hands.

keyTerms.meaning: A betrothed woman: after קידושין but before full marriage
A fully married woman, after נישואין
The matter became clear; it turned out that

phrases.english: In the end the matter became clear
that she was a betrothed woman.
רבא said:
If they said this about a married woman,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the rule רב עיליש used: whatever a wife acquires belongs to her husband.

phrases.english: would they say it about a betrothed woman?!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְסוֹף אִיגַּלַּי מִילְּתָא דַּאֲרוּסָה הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב עיליש's challenge from step 9 based on the facts of the case
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the challenge to a different case: the husband's rights only apply to a נשואה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The place the woman acquired automatically belongs to the husband, so the גט never left his hands
steps.terutzMaskana: For an ארוסה the husband gets nothing she acquires, so the spot and the גט are truly hers

steps.title: רבא: for any wife, the גט and the courtyard arrive together
steps.stepSummary: רבא changes his answer: it makes no difference whether she is an ארוסה or a נשואה, because her גט and her courtyard come to her at the same moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא then said: It makes no difference whether she is betrothed or married. Her גט and her courtyard come to her together.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a stronger answer that works even for a fully married woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband only gets what his wife acquires while she is still his wife. The moment she acquires the courtyard is the same moment the גט takes effect and she stops being his wife. So the husband never has a chance to take the courtyard, and the גט works.

keyTerms.meaning: He then said again; he took back or improved his earlier answer
Come together at the same moment

steps.whatToRemember: גיטה וחצירה באין כאחד: the גט and the courtyard reach the wife together, so the husband's right to her acquisitions never takes hold of the courtyard.

phrases.english: רבא then said:
It makes no difference whether she is betrothed
and no difference whether she is married —
her גט and her courtyard come together at once.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אָמַר רָבָא: לָא שְׁנָא אֲרוּסָה וְלָא שְׁנָא נְשׂוּאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Broadens the answer of step 10 so it covers a נשואה too
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Any wife, betrothed or married, can be divorced through a place that is given to her, because the place and the גט reach her together.

steps.title: Didn't רבא already say this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא needed to say 'her גט and her courtyard come together' here, when he already said it earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבא already said this at the start!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that this rule of רבא was already quoted earlier, so it seems repeated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back in step 4, רבא himself already said this very idea: 'her גט and her courtyard come together.' So why does the story show רבא coming up with it only now? The גמרא wants to know how these two pieces fit.

phrases.english: But רבא already said this at the start!
phrases.notes: Back in step 4, רבא himself said 'her גט and her courtyard come together.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אַמְרַהּ רָבָא מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why רבא's statement in step 11 repeats what was said earlier
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's statement that the גט and the courtyard come together
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבא already held this rule, why does it appear as a new idea in this story?

steps.title: רבא said it in this very story
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the earlier quote of רבא is the same statement. He said it about this story.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבא said it, he said it about this very incident.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there are not two statements. This story is where רבא's rule came from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule רבא stated in step 4 is not a separate teaching. It is the same rule רבא first said here, after רב עיליש's challenge. So nothing is repeated.

phrases.english: When רבא said it —
he said it about this incident.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אַמְרַהּ רָבָא אַהַאי מַעֲשֶׂה אַמְרַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing it is one and the same statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא said the rule twice, which seems unnecessary
steps.terutzMaskana: The earlier quote comes from this story; it was said only once

steps.title: עולא: she must be next to her house or courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's words 'and she is in her house.' עולא says this only works if she is standing near her house and courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says 'and she is in her house.' עולא said: This is only when she is standing next to her house and next to her courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts. The גמרא quotes words from the משנה, and עולא explains how close the woman must be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that if the husband throws the גט into her house or courtyard, she is divorced. עולא reads 'she is in her house' strictly: she must be right there by her house or courtyard. Only then does the place take the גט for her.

keyTerms.meaning: Courtyard; a person's property can acquire things for its owner

phrases.english: 'And she is in her house.'
phrases.notes: These words come from the משנה. The גמרא is going back to explain them.

phrases.english: עולא said:
This is only when she is standing
next to her house and next to her courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִיא בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתָהּ. אָמַר עוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section that explains a phrase in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A courtyard receives a גט for the woman only if she is standing next to it.

steps.title: רבי אושעיא: she can even be in another city
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא disagrees with עולא. Even if she is in טבריא and her courtyard is in ציפורי, or the other way around, she is divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא said: Even if she is in טבריא and her courtyard is in ציפורי, or she is in ציפורי and her courtyard is in טבריא, she is divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אושעיא gives the opposite view: she does not need to be near the courtyard at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אושעיא, the courtyard acquires for her no matter where she is. טבריא and ציפורי are two separate cities, so being nearby does not matter. This directly disagrees with עולא's requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: Tiberias, a city in the גליל
Tzippori, a different city in the גליל

phrases.english: רבי אושעיא said:
Even if she is in טבריא
and her courtyard is in ציפורי;
or she is in ציפורי and her courtyard is in טבריא —
she is divorced.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ הִיא בִּטְבֶרְיָא וַחֲצֵרָהּ בְּצִיפּוֹרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the view that disagrees with עולא in step 14
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Her courtyard acquires the גט for her even when she is far away in another city.

steps.title: But the משנה says she is in her house
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אושעיא: the משנה clearly says 'she is in her house and in her courtyard.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה teaches 'she is in her house and in her courtyard'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי אושעיא using the plain words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's wording sounds like she must actually be there, which fits עולא. If she can be in another city, why would the משנה say she is in her house?

phrases.english: But 'she is in her house
and in her courtyard' is what the משנה teaches!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא הִיא בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתָהּ וּבְתוֹךְ חֲצֵרָהּ קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אושעיא's view from step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אושעיא's ruling that she can be in another city
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's words say she is inside her house and courtyard, which sounds like she must be there in person

steps.title: The משנה means 'as if she were in her house'
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the משנה means she is treated as if she were in her house or courtyard, because a courtyard guarded for her acts on her behalf.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means: 'She is like someone who is in her house'; 'she is like someone who is in her courtyard.' Since the courtyard is guarded with her knowledge, she is divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אושעיא by reading the משנה's words differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'In her house' does not mean she is physically there. It means her house counts as if she were there. A courtyard that is guarded with her knowledge (a guarded courtyard) acts for her even from far away, so the גט works.

keyTerms.meaning: Guarded with her knowledge; kept safe for her

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אושעיא, a courtyard that is guarded for the woman can receive her גט even if she is in another city. The משנה's 'in her house' means 'as if she were in her house.'
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'she is in her house' as a physical requirement here. The גמרא explains it as 'as if she were in her house,' so that it fits רבי אושעיא.

phrases.english: This is what it means:
'And she is like someone who is in her house';
'and she is like someone who is in her courtyard' —
because since it is a courtyard that is guarded
with her knowledge,
she is divorced.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: וְהִיא כְּמִי שֶׁבְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16 and keeps רבי אושעיא's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה requires her to be physically inside her house or courtyard
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means she is treated as if she were there, because a guarded courtyard acts for her

steps.title: Maybe they argue about why a courtyard works
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that עולא and רבי אושעיא disagree about why a חצר can receive a גט. One says it works as her hand. The other says it works as her agent.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is their argument: one holds a courtyard counts because it is like her hand, and the other holds a courtyard counts because it is like an agent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible reason behind the argument between עולא and רבי אושעיא. This is a suggestion, and the next step will test it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a חצר is like her hand, it makes sense that it must be close to her, like עולא said. If a חצר is like an agent (שליח), it can act for her even from far away, like רבי אושעיא said. So this suggestion ties each opinion to a different basic reason.

keyTerms.meaning: because of her hand (the courtyard counts as her hand)

phrases.english: Let us say that they disagree about this:

phrases.aramaic: דְּמָר סָבַר: חָצֵר מִשּׁוּם יָדָהּ אִתְרַבַּאי;
phrases.english: that one master holds: a courtyard was included because of her hand;
phrases.notes: 'One master' is עולא, who said she must be near her courtyard.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: חָצֵר מִשּׁוּם שְׁלִיחוּת אִתְרַבַּאי?
phrases.english: and the other master holds: a courtyard was included because of agency?
phrases.notes: This is רבי אושעיא. An agent can act for you even when you are far away.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא בְּהָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the root reason behind the argument between עולא and רבי אושעיא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the argument about whether חצר works as יד or as שליחות?

steps.title: No, both agree it is like her hand; for עולא it must be near her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Everyone agrees a חצר works as her hand. עולא learns from this that the courtyard must be next to her, just like a hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees a courtyard counts because it is like her hand. One master says: like her hand. Just as her hand is next to her, so too her courtyard must be next to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the suggestion from step 18. It explains עולא's view in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is no longer יד versus שליחות. Both sides agree on יד. עולא takes the comparison to mean the courtyard must be close to her, because a hand is always close to its owner.

phrases.english: No; everyone agrees:
a courtyard was included because of her hand;
one master holds: like her hand:
just as her hand is next to her,
so too her courtyard works when it is next to her.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא; דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 18's explanation and offers a different reason for the argument
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that either side holds חצר works through שליחות
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both opinions can be explained with חצר as יד; they differ only in how the comparison to a hand is applied

steps.title: For רבי אושעיא, the comparison means the courtyard must be guarded with her knowledge
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא argues that עולא's comparison goes too far, since then the courtyard would also have to be attached to her. Instead, a hand is guarded with her knowledge, so the courtyard must be guarded with her knowledge.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one says: if so, just as her hand is attached to her, should her courtyard have to be attached too?! Rather, like her hand: just as her hand is guarded with her knowledge, so too her courtyard that is guarded with her knowledge. This leaves out a courtyard of hers that is guarded without her knowledge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי אושעיא's side of the comparison to a hand. This finishes the new explanation of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אושעיא shows that you cannot copy every feature of a hand. A courtyard can never be physically attached to a person. So he picks a different shared feature: she watches over both of them. That is why distance does not matter to him, only her control.
steps.whatToRemember: Both עולא and רבי אושעיא agree a חצר works like her hand. עולא says the courtyard must be near her. רבי אושעיא says it must be guarded with her knowledge, even if it is far away.

phrases.english: And the other one:
phrases.notes: This is רבי אושעיא, explaining why he does not accept עולא's comparison.

phrases.english: if so, just as her hand is attached,
so too her courtyard must be attached?!
Rather, like her hand:
just as her hand is guarded with her knowledge,
so too her courtyard that is guarded with her knowledge;
to exclude her courtyard that is guarded not with her knowledge.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ – אִי, מָה יָדָהּ בִּדְבוּקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the new explanation by giving רבי אושעיא's reading of 'like her hand'
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each side reads the comparison to a hand differently
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Comparing the courtyard to a hand would mean it must be close to her, like a hand
steps.terutzMaskana: The shared feature is being guarded with her knowledge, so a far-away courtyard she controls still works

steps.title: A גט thrown into a courtyard lands on a board
steps.stepSummary: A man threw a גט to his wife while she stood in a courtyard. The גט landed on a wooden board inside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man threw a גט to his wife. She was standing in a courtyard. The גט went and fell onto a board.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story. This step sets up the question that רב יוסף answers next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether the board counts as part of her courtyard. If it does, she is divorced. If it does not, she is not. The text does not ask this out loud, but the next step answers it.

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דִּזְרַק לַהּ גִּיטָּא לִדְבֵיתְהוּ.
phrases.english: A certain man threw a get to his wife.
She was standing in a courtyard.
The get went and fell onto a board.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דִּזְרַק לַהּ גִּיטָּא לִדְבֵיתְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new practical case about a גט thrown into a courtyard
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a board inside the courtyard count as part of her חצר?

steps.title: רב יוסף: a board of four by four אמות is its own domain
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rules that if the board is ארבע אמות by ארבע אמות, it is its own separate רשות. If it is smaller, it is part of the courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: We look. If the board is four cubits by four cubits, it makes a separate domain for itself. If not, it is all one domain.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the case from step 21 by measuring the board.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A large board of ארבע אמות by ארבע אמות counts as its own place. So the גט did not land in her courtyard, and she is not divorced. A smaller board is just part of the courtyard, so the גט reached her חצר and she is divorced.
steps.whatToRemember: A board inside a courtyard counts as a separate רשות only if it is at least ארבע אמות by ארבע אמות. Otherwise it is part of the courtyard.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: We look:

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָוְיָא אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת עַל אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת –
phrases.english: if it is four cubits by four cubits,
phrases.notes: 'It' means the board the גט landed on.

phrases.english: it divides off a domain for itself;
and if not, it is one domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: חָזֵינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling on the board case
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A board of at least four by four אמות is a separate domain; a smaller one is part of the courtyard

steps.title: Whose courtyard is it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יוסף's ruling. Whether the courtyard belongs to the wife or to the husband, the size of the board should make no difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we talking about? If it is her courtyard, then even if the board is four אמות, so what? It is still hers. If it is his courtyard, then even if the board is smaller than four אמות, so what? None of it is hers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what case רב יוסף was talking about. It shows that his rule seems pointless either way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the courtyard is hers, the board is also hers, so the גט should work even if the board is a separate רשות. If the courtyard is his, she owns none of it, so the גט should fail even if the board is small. In both cases the four-אמות size test seems to change nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with?
What of it? (it makes no difference)

phrases.english: With what are we dealing?
If we say it is in her own courtyard,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָוֵי אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת מַאי הָוֵי?
phrases.english: then if the board was four cubits, what of it?
Rather, say it is in his courtyard,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי לָא הָוֵי אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת מַאי הָוֵי?
phrases.english: then even if it was not four cubits, what of it?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? אִילֵימָא בְּחָצֵר דִּידַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of רב יוסף given in step 22
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A two-sided challenge. In either possible case (her courtyard or his), the size of the board should not affect whether the גט works.

steps.title: He lent her the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The case is his courtyard, which he lent her so she could receive the גט. People lend one place, not two, so a board that is its own רשות was not included in the loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the ruling is needed where he lent her the place. People usually lend one place, but they do not lend two places.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The courtyard is his, but he lent it to her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since he lent her the courtyard, it works for her to receive the גט. A loan normally covers only one area. A board of four אמות counts as a second, separate area, so it was not lent to her and the גט does not work there. A smaller board is just part of the courtyard, so it was included.

keyTerms.meaning: No, it is needed (for a specific case)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows why the size of the board matters. It decides whether the board counts as one place with the courtyard, or as a second place that was not lent.

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where he lent her the place;
for people lend one place,
but people do not lend two places.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּאוֹשְׁלַהּ מָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two-sided challenge of step 23
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines a specific case: his courtyard, lent to her
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The courtyard is simply either hers or his, so size should not matter
steps.terutzMaskana: It is his courtyard lent to her. The loan covers only one place, so a separate four-אמות board is not included.

steps.title: A board ten טפחים high is separate even if small
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits רב יוסף's rule. The four-אמות test applies only to a board lower than ten טפחים. A board ten טפחים high is a separate רשות even if it is small.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only said this when the board is not ten high. But if it is ten high, it is a separate place even though it is not four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to רב יוסף's rule about the board's size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Height can also make a place separate. If the board is ten טפחים higher than the courtyard, it is its own רשות even when it is smaller than four אמות. A גט landing there would not be in the lent courtyard.

phrases.english: And we said this only
where it is not ten high,
phrases.notes: Ten means ten טפחים (handbreadths) above the courtyard floor.

phrases.english: but if it is ten high,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא הָוֵי אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת.
phrases.english: even though it is not four cubits, it is separate.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלֹא גָּבוֹהַּ עֲשָׂרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to רב יוסף's rule now that it has been explained
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A board ten טפחים high is a separate רשות even if smaller than four אמות.

steps.title: A second limit begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a second limit on רב יוסף's rule, about a board that does not have some feature. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we only said this when it does not have...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a second limit on the rule. The sentence finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same opening words, וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא, show that another condition is coming. We do not yet know what the board must lack. The next lines will tell us.

phrases.english: And we said this only where it does not have

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלֵית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second limit, using the same formula as step 25
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Incomplete here. A further condition on רב יוסף's rule is being introduced.
